after.title: Preprint: Revisiting the First Night Effect of Polysomnography Using Wearable EEG Headbands in Older Adults with Sleep Disturbances
after.authors: Chen, A.; Cho, G.; Murphy, I.; Asamoah-Mensah, M.; Talarczyk, J.; Miner, B.
after.abstract: Study Objectives: The first night effect (FNE), where sleep is altered during the first night of polysomnography (PSG), may affect the validity of single-night PSG assessments, yet its magnitude relative to habitual sleep is difficult to characterize using repeated PSG alone. We examined FNE during home-based PSG (HPSG) in older adults with sleep disturbances using multi-night wearable EEG headband (HB) recordings. Methods: Fifty-eight community-dwelling adults aged 55-85 years with sleep disturbances completed up to seven nights of HB monitoring, including one night of simultaneous HPSG. Using HB-derived measures, we compared total sleep time (TST), wake after sleep onset (WASO), sleep efficiency (SE), minutes in N3 sleep, and minutes in REM sleep between HPSG and non-HPSG nights via pairwise comparisons and linear mixed-effects models adjusting for age, sex, and race/ethnicity. Results: Sleep differed significantly between HPSG and non-HPSG nights, with roughly 35 minutes longer WASO, 21 minutes less N3 sleep, and 15% lower SE (ps < .001) during HPSG nights. TST and REM sleep did not differ between HPSG and non-HPSG nights. Findings were consistent when separately comparing nights preceding and following HPSG. Conclusions: In older adults with sleep disturbances, a single night of HPSG was associated with greater wake after sleep onset, less N3 sleep, and lower sleep efficiency than other nights measured with wearable EEG, suggesting that one-night PSG may overstate sleep disruption and understate deep sleep. Multi-night wearable EEG monitoring may help assess the representativeness of single-night PSG measurements, thereby improving the accuracy of sleep measurement interpretation.

after.authors: Miyake, F.; Watari, T.; Kosaka, S.; Goto, Y.; Edagawa, N.; Takayama, T.; Ishida, K.; So, R.; Kataoka, Y.
after.abstract: Objectives: We aimed to assess agreement between reviewers in factor extraction and Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) classification, and between large language model (LLM) classifications and reviewer-consensus reference standards, using public medical incident reports from Japan. Methods: Six clinicians in three pairs reviewed 150 records with artificial intelligence (AI)-generated fault tree analysis (FTA) candidates and 60 new records without AI candidates, creating pair-consensus reference standards (RSv1 and RSv2). We assessed classification agreement, factor-extraction micro-F1, and FTA versus direct classification. Reviewers reassessed RSv2 after additional public information. AI classification was also evaluated on fixed RSv2 factors. Results: Pooled inter-reviewer detailed-category kappa in RSv1 was 0.503 (95% CI, 0.456 to 0.548). In the final RSv1 evaluation (37 records; 306 leaves), kappa was 0.427 (0.359 to 0.493) for GPT-5.6 Sol and 0.499 (0.445 to 0.551) for secondary Kimi K2.6. Neither estimate reached the detailed-category kappa target of 0.6. FTA-based structural rankings and factor-frequency rankings selected identical top-five categories; the FTA-minus-direct-classification micro-F1 difference was 0.032 (-0.024 to 0.086). RSv2 factor-extraction micro-F1 was 0.420 (0.303 to 0.527), using AI-assisted semantic matching; 23/60 RSv2 records were analysable with uncertainty and 22/60 were not analysable. Responses without uncertainty accounted for 37.5% before and 46.7% after reassessment; pooled linear weighted kappa for inter-reviewer analysability agreement was 0.386 and 0.203. Exploratory AI classification of 75 RSv2 factors with a single HFACS label yielded detailed-category kappa 0.240 (0.101 to 0.390). Conclusions: Disagreement persisted in the extraction and classification of contributing factors from public medical incident reports, including in reviewer assessments, and the tested FTA approach did not establish added value. Difficulty obtaining sufficiently specific contextual information from the available narratives may have contributed to these judgement difficulties, consistent with concerns raised in previous studies. Organisations that operate incident reporting systems or develop reporting guidance could strengthen reporting processes so that the specific circumstances and context needed to interpret contributing factors and relationships are recorded.

after.authors: Tubeti, M.; Michael, D.; Konje, E.; Todd, J.; Malindisa, E.
after.abstract: Background: High blood pressure (BP) is a serious public health concern worldwide, including Tanzania, due to its impact in cardiovascular diseases. Among people living with HIV (PLHIV) high blood pressure has been linked with some anti-retroviral therapy (ART) regimens. Since its introduction in 2018, dolutegravir (DTG) has achieved a high rate of viral suppression compared to previous ART regimens. However, clinical and epidemiological studies have associated DTG with weight gain and other adiposity measures, which may increase the risk of high blood pressure and cardiovascular diseases. Method: Between June 2016 and May 2021 500 adults PLHIV were started on ART, with BP, body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-height ratio (WtHR) measured at initiation and at regular follow-ups. Trends in BP, BMI, and WtHR were described using line graphs. Changes in BP, BMI and WtHR, and 95% confidence intervals (95%CI), associated with DTG or other ART regimes were assessed using mixed-effects linear regression models, with patients as clusters. Results: DTG was significantly associated with increase in BMI (coefficient=0.03, p=0.001, 95%CI=0.02-0.04) after adjusted for age and sex compared to other ART. DTG was not significantly associated with change in systolic BP compared with other ART regimens (coefficient=0.003, p=0.886, 95% CI:-0.04 to 0.05) after adjustment for BMI, age and sex. Conclusion: DTG was associated with greater increases in BMI compared to other ART regimens but after adjusting for BMI was not independently linked to higher systolic blood pressure. The absence of an association between DTG and SBP after adjustment for BMI suggests that differences in adiposity may partly account for the observed crude association.

We evaluated the efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety of a bivalent EVA71-CVA16 vaccine. Methods In this multicenter, double-blind, phase 3 trial, 8,000 healthy children aged 6-71 months were randomly assigned (1:1) to two doses of the bivalent or a licensed EVA71 vaccine, 1 month apart. The primary efficacy endpoint was RT-PCR-confirmed CVA16-associated HFMD with onset at least 14 days after dose 2. EVA71 immunogenicity noninferiority was assessed among baseline-seronegative participants without previous EVA71 vaccination. Results Of 7,975 participants receiving at least one dose, 7,419 underwent the primary efficacy analysis. CVA16-associated HFMD occurred in 4 bivalent-group versus 44 EVA71-group participants (vaccine efficacy, 90.91%; 95% CI, 75.03-97.63). At 30 days after dose 2, the EVA71 geometric mean titer (GMT) ratio was 2.04 (95% CI, 1.71-2.44) among baseline-seronegative participants without previous EVA71 vaccination. In the humoral immunogenicity population at this time point, CVA16 seroconversion rates were 96.94% versus 8.68%, and GMTs were 918.96 versus 3.88 U/mL. after.abstract: The burden of dementia is rising rapidly, but preventive strategies remain limited and few tools exist to identify individuals at risk a priori. This unmet need is especially relevant in atrial fibrillation (AF), a rapidly growing population at increased risk of dementia. We present MIND-AF, an AI-based model to predict 3 to 5-year risk of dementia from readily available bedside data. Developed in 108,672 AF patients without prior dementia within an academic-community network in California, MIND-AF predicted incident dementia in a held-out test cohort (n=32,238) with a C-index of 0.82 over 3.8 +/- 4.6 years after AF diagnosis, outperforming age and clinical risk scores (CHA2DS2-VASc, HATCH; all p < 0.001). MIND-AF enabled a priori stratification into low, medium and high-risk groups, with dementia incidence of 0.34%, 1.59% and 6.3% over 3 years and 0.7%, 3.4% and 13.0% over 5 years from AF diagnosis, respectively. MIND-AF provided similar performance in a sealed external population of 58,826 demographically distinct patients in Georgia (C-index 0.80), as well as pre-specified cohorts without neurodegenerative disease, mild cognitive impairment, stroke or transient ischemic attack. MIND-AF, freely available as an online web application, provides scalable point-of-care risk stratification for incident dementia in patients diagnosed with AF, is robust to baseline neurocognitive and cerebrovascular baseline states, and provides a bedside framework for intensified dementia prevention.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Chair of Biological Imaging, Central Institute for Translational Cancer Research (TranslaTUM), School of Medicine and Health & School of Computation, Informatio
after.abstract: Despite transformative advances in continuous glucose monitoring, current continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) still relies on transcutaneous needle-based sensors that measure glucose in the interstitial fluid, which lags behind blood glucose. Mid-infrared optoacoustic sensing (MiROS) has recently demonstrated a sensitivity to glucose changes of a few tens of mg/dL in mice using non-invasive measurements. However, the relation of MiROS to human measurements remains unknown. We conducted a MiROS pilot study in 30 healthy participants undergoing oral glucose tolerance tests and investigated how optoacoustic signals reflect tissue optical-property variations associated with changes in blood glucose concentration. We defined the Optoacoustic Mid-infrared Signal (OMS) as a readout of glucose-induced alterations in tissue optical properties and compared it with reference blood glucose measurements. The OMS corresponded to a mean absolute error (MAE) of 11.9 mg/dL and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 10% relative to the reference blood analysis. More than 99.9% of paired OMS values were located in zones A and B of the consensus error grid. The study further showed that OMS compared favourably with concurrently acquired CGM measurements, which showed an MAE of 15.7 mg/dL and a MAPE of 12% and exhibited an average time lag of 10.5 min relative to blood glucose. No comparable lag was observed for the OMS. These results support MiROS as a promising framework pointing to a sensor with potential for non-invasive glucose sensing in humans, in the future, and a potential step toward less burdensome glucose monitoring for diabetes management.

after.title: Preprint: Place or placeholder? AlphaEarth satellite embeddings did not detectably improve weekly dengue forecasts in four countries
after.authors: Patel, B. K.; Asokan, A. V.; Pant, S.
after.abstract: Background. Some recent disease forecasts use satellite embeddings (numbers summarising places). A model may use them only as a placeholder, recognising districts and their usual dengue levels without learning about the environment. We asked whether AlphaEarth embeddings improve weekly district dengue forecasts and whether gains go beyond such recognition. Methods. We retrospectively forecast cases one and four weeks ahead in 6,909 districts of Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Taiwan (OpenDengue, 2020-2024) with gradient boosting. In 14 comparisons across future years and held-out places, we measured how embeddings changed the weighted interval score, with and without a location control (an input that only identifies a district), to test whether location alone explains gains. We used Diebold-Mariano tests, the Holm correction and a +/-1% equivalence margin set after the first Brazil and Peru results. Findings. No comparison showed a significant gain after correction. Six showed losses: five small (-0.42% to -0.68%) and one with Taiwan held out (-18.3%; absolute -0.0037). Only Colombia's held-out-states loss (-0.52%) stayed significant under two stricter checks and a check for cases hidden in zero-filled weeks. In 8 comparisons (5 under the stricter checks), any gain or loss was shown to be smaller than 1% of forecast error. This margin is roughly Brazil's gain from all non-case inputs combined. In exploratory analyses, embeddings alone predicted district burden in unseen states. Without case history, neither coordinates nor embeddings helped detectably in Brazil's held-out states; both hurt in Colombia's. In Brazil's future years, coordinates cut error by 3.3% (1.7 to 4.9); embeddings added nothing detectable. Interpretation. Embeddings partly showed which districts usually have more dengue, but in Brazil and Colombia other non-case inputs already held most of it. With case history they added no detectable accuracy; without it, evidence was inconclusive. Embeddings should be tested against location-only controls in held-out places.

after.authors: Lazarides, C.; Fiedler, J.; Klos, L.; Volk, C.; Niessner, C.; Voelkle, M.; Woll, A.
after.abstract: Background: Evidence in youth on whether pandemic-related changes in physical activity (PA), recreational screen time (ST), and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) persisted after the COVID-19 pandemic is limited. In a longitudinal study, we examined changes from pre- to post-pandemic and whether these changes differed by age at pre-pandemic. Methods: Longitudinal data were obtained from 945 participants (49% female) aged 4-17 years pre-pandemic in the German Motorik-Modul Study. HRQoL, ST, everyday PA, and the number of days per week with at least 60 minutes of PA (WHO PA days) were assessed pre-pandemic (2018-2020), during both German lockdowns (2020 and 2021), and post-pandemic after restrictions ended (2023). Covariate-adjusted random-intercept mixed-effects models tested pre- to post-pandemic changes and moderation by baseline age. Lockdown trajectories were explored using successive contrasts. Results: Compared with pre-pandemic levels, post-pandemic HRQoL decreased (B = -5.92, 95% CI [-6.82, -5.03]), everyday PA decreased by 31.15 minutes per day (95% CI [-36.40, -25.91]), and WHO PA days decreased by 0.27 days per week (95% CI [-0.43, -0.11]). ST increased by 75.17 minutes per day (95% CI [66.65, 83.69]; all p < .001). Age moderated changes in HRQoL, ST, and everyday PA, but not WHO PA days. Children aged 6-13 years showed the greatest ST increases. Children younger than 11 years showed the largest everyday PA declines. Additionally explored trajectories varied across lockdowns and were moderated by age prior to the pandemic. Conclusions: Childrens and adolescents PA, ST, and HRQoL had not returned to pre-pandemic levels one year after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted. Developmentally tailored monitoring and interventions may be required, particularly for younger and school-aged children in face of ongoing global crises.

after.authors: Baggio, S.; Gautier, M.; Radunz, M.; Galanis, C. R.; Stevens, M. W. R.; Khanna, D.; Billieux, J.; Starcevic, V.; Lindenberg, K.; Wade, T.; King, D. L.
after.abstract: Background. Australia was the first country to adopt a national minimum age requirement for social media use. This policy has been widely debated, and evidence is only just starting to emerge about its impacts on adolescents. This study examined the effect of the social media ban on psychological distress, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and the impact on daily life and academic self-efficacy. Methods. We conducted an emulated trial using follow-up data collected three months after the ban implementation from a two-wave survey of South Australian high school students aged 12 to 15 (N=551). Exposure was defined as adherence to the ban, which was assessed in two ways: strictly (self-reported adherence combined with reported social media behaviours), and less strictly (self-report only). The primary outcome was the Revised Children's Anxiety and Depression Scale (RCADS-11). Secondary outcomes included RCADS-11 impact subscore; Child Health Utility 9 Dimensions (CHU9D) utility score (HRQoL); score of CHU9D activity-related items, which assessed daily functioning; and the academic self-efficacy subscale of the Self-Efficacy Questionnaire for Children (SEQ-C). Adjusted regression models were performed using inverse probability weighting to account for group imbalance and attrition. Findings. Using the strict definition, 14.8% of adolescents adhered to the ban, compared to 41.5% under the less stringent definition. Adherence had no significant effect on the RCADS-11 total score or impact subscore (p[≥].321). Those who adhered to the ban had significantly higher HRQoL, better daily functioning and higher academic self-efficacy (p[≤].033). Overall, effects were small in magnitude. No significant effects were observed under the less stringent definition of adherence (p=.244). Interpretation. Strict adherence to the social media ban was associated with minor short-term improvements in HRQoL and daily functioning, but not psychological distress. Funding. This research was supported by a Channel 7 Children's Research Foundation grant.

after.abstract: Abstract: Background Cardiometabolic dysregulation and depression frequently co-occur, yet studies often assume linear biomarker and depression relationships and under-represent South Asian populations. We investigated linear and non-linear associations between cardiometabolic biomarkers and electronic health record (EHR) derived depression in British Bangladeshi and British Pakistani adults. Methods We analysed Genes & Health data across five EHR biomarkers: body mass index (BMI), glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and triglycerides. In a primary development cohort (N = 6,340; 1,585 cases matched 1:3 to 4,755 controls), we applied principal component analysis and sex- and ethnicity-adjusted logistic regression to compare linear, restricted cubic spline, and optimised hybrid models. Models were validated externally in two temporal holdout sets sharing 18,733 controls: Holdout Set 1 (281 cases measured 6 to 12 months pre-diagnosis; N = 19,014) and Holdout Set 2 (1,815 cases measured >12 months pre-diagnosis; N = 20,548). Results Depression cases exhibited higher median HbA1c and lower LDL cholesterol in both ethnic groups, alongside higher BMI and triglycerides among Pakistani participants (all p < 0.05). The first three principal components explained 72.7% of metabolic variance with extensive ethnic overlap. Splines revealed non-linear trajectories, including a J-shaped curve for HbA1c and a U-shaped curve for LDL cholesterol. Relative to the linear model (C index = 0.6219; Nagelkerke R2 = 0.0557), both the full spline (C index = 0.6542; R2 = 0.0849; p < 0.0001) and optimised hybrid models retaining linear HbA1c (C-index = 0.6514; R2 = 0.0826; p < 0.0001) substantially improved fit, discrimination and calibration. External discrimination remained superior in Holdout Set 1 (AUC = 0.6229 - 0.6230 vs 0.5793 linear) but attenuated in Holdout Set 2 (AUC = 0.5295 - 0.5354 vs 0.5231 linear). Conclusions Cardiometabolic biomarkers exhibit distinct non-linear relationships with depression in British South Asian adults, particularly within 12 months of diagnosis. Incorporating biomarker-specific functional forms significantly improves model performance over conventional linear approaches.

after.authors: McCoy, B.; Ali, A.; Bell, L.; Carter, B.; Wang, K.; Yan, P.; Jin, H.; Elise, F.; Acton, D.; Jaydeokar, S.; Gore, N.; Chinn, D.; Hassiotis, A.; Strydom, A.; Shetty, H.; Downs, J.; Stewart, R.; Sheehan, R.
after.abstract: Background Care (Education) and Treatment Reviews (C(E)TRs) were introduced in 2015 to prevent unnecessary hospital admissions amongst people with intellectual disability and autistic people. Little is known about people who receive community C(E)TRs or the effectiveness of community C(E)TRs in reducing admissions. Aims To estimate the causal effect of community C(E)TRs on psychiatric hospital admission, and compare length of hospital stay between patients who did and did not have a pre-admission community C(E)TR. Method We conducted a retrospective observational study using de-identified electronic health record data from 2,495 patients. We characterised the sociodemographic and clinical profiles of people with intellectual disability and autistic people who received a community C(E)TR between 2015 and 2025. We used propensity score weighting and a difference-in-differences analysis to compare changes in psychiatric hospital admissions in the six months before and after community C(E)TRs, with changes over corresponding periods in matched controls. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to compare lengths of hospital stay between patients who had a pre-admission C(E)TR and those who did not. Results 446 community C(E)TRs were identified in the intellectual disability group and 382 in the autistic group. The intellectual disability group had a median age of 21 years and were predominately male (60.7%) whereas the autistic group were younger (median age 16 years) with a higher proportion of females (55.2%). Community C(E)TRs reduced the odds of psychiatric hospital admission over six months compared with controls (pooled OR = 0.47, 95% CI 0.26-0.85) but there was no difference over 12 months (pooled OR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.48-1.35). Length of hospital stay did not differ between those with and without a pre-admission C(E)TR. Conclusions These findings suggest that C(E)TRs may delay rather than prevent admissions and highlight the need for adequately resourced, sustainable community services to support people at high risk of admission.

after.title: Preprint: Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems Use and Reduced Days of Cigarette Smoking: A Causal Bayesian Additive Regression Tree Analysis of Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study Waves 4 to 6
after.authors: Xu, S.; Hill, J.; Cui, L.; Feng, Y.; Niaura, R. S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: School of Global Public Health, New York University
after.abstract: Background. Debate persists regarding the potential harm reduction role of Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS). This study estimated the effect of ENDS use on subsequent cigarette smoking days in the past 30 days among adult smokers. Methods. We analyzed longitudinal data from Waves 4 to 6 of the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health (PATH) Study, including 4,909 established current smokers. Bayesian Additive Regression Trees for causal inference was used to estimate the average exposure effect (ATE) of current ENDS use (characterized as no use, some-day use, and daily use) at Wave 5 (2018 - 2019) on cigarette smoking days at Wave 6 (2021), adjusting for 26 covariates measured at Wave 4 (2016 - 2018). Results. Compared with no ENDS use, daily ENDS use reduced cigarette smoking by 6.17 days per month over a two-year period (ATE = -6.17, 95% CI: -8.16 to -5.29); whereas some-day use reduced smoking by 0.99 days (ATE = -0.99, 95% CI: -1.65 to -0.28). Compared with some-day use, daily ENDS users reduced smoking by 5.65 days per month (ATE = -5.65, 95% CI: -6.72 to -4.72). There was no evidence that these effects differed meaningfully across demographic or psychosocial subgroups. Conclusions. Among established adult smokers, daily ENDS use reduced subsequent smoking days compared with some-day and no ENDS use. These findings support the potential role of ENDS as a harm reduction strategy for adult smokers while highlighting the need for better characterizing behavioral patterns and health consequences associated with sustained ENDS use.

after.title: Preprint: Synthetic Magnetic Resonance Spectra Generation using convex NMF in Neuro-Oncology
after.authors: Mac Carthaigh, M.; Toth, L. F.; Vellido, A.; Julia-Sape, M.
after.abstract: Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy is a powerful, non-invasive technique for investigating the metabolic composition of biological tissues, particularly useful in the classification of brain tumours. However, its inclusion into machine learning pipelines is limited by the scarcity of large, labelled datasets. This work evaluates whether synthetic MR spectra generated using convex Non-negative Matrix Factorisation and probabilistic modelling of the resulting weight distributions can improve brain tumour classification. MR spectra from the INTERPRET database were decomposed into interpretable source and weight matrices, both separately for each of six diagnostic tasks and jointly across five tissue classes, at short and long echo time. Class-specific weight distributions were modelled using Gaussian Mixture Models and Kernel Density Estimation across a range of hyperparameter settings, and new weight vectors were sampled and recombined with the fixed source matrix to produce synthetic spectra; hyperparameters were selected by the mean squared error to the real class means. The diagnostic utility of the synthetic spectra was assessed with Linear Discriminant Analysis under three internal and four external evaluation strategies, the latter using an independent multi-centre cohort. Synthetic spectra were readily classified by models trained on real data (mean accuracy 0.87), but models trained on synthetic spectra alone generalised poorly, both to real INTERPRET spectra (0.55) and to the external cohort (0.47, against 0.84 for training on real data; p [≤] 0.003). Augmenting real training data with synthetic spectra neither improved nor significantly harmed external accuracy (mean paired differences between -0.04 and +0.01; all p [≥] 0.027 uncorrected, none significant after correction), and class-balanced augmentation did not help, and task-specific and joint decompositions performed comparably. The selected generative models were low in complexity and produced spectra closer to the class means than the real data are, suggesting that selection by reconstruction fidelity is poorly aligned with the goal of augmentation, and that internal validation alone would have overstated the value of the synthetic data.

data.summary: added: Preprint: Clinical medicine admission cutoffs in China, 2017-2026: a coverage-sensitive national longitudinal analysis

after.title: Preprint: Clinical medicine admission cutoffs in China, 2017-2026: a coverage-sensitive national longitudinal analysis
after.authors: Zhou, H.; Li, X.
after.abstract: Context. Clinical medicine cutoffs locate published score or rank boundaries at filing or admission. China's 31 provincial systems support a ten-year national analysis of these boundaries and their career context. Methods. Undergraduate clinical medicine cutoffs were identified in examination cohorts across the 31 provincial systems from 2017 to 2026. The estimand was the unweighted mean of provincial median school cutoffs. Filing and admission stages were not consistently distinguished. Schools and pathways were compared at matched endpoints under alternative school identities. Comparisons beginning at the 2023 maximum were post hoc and descriptive. Results. Of 310 province-year cells, 262 met the three-school threshold. Among 407 province-school pairs observed throughout the decade, mean percentiles were 76.23 in 2017, 86.06 in 2023 and 76.51 in 2026. Across 754 endpoint pairs, the matched-school change was +3.02 points. School and province coverage expansion changed the estimate by -6.44 and -0.49 points, yielding -3.90. In 2023-2025, provincial medians moved later in 25 of 29 provinces and earlier in four; mean change was -2.31 points (2,084 pairs; 95% interval -3.36 to -1.25). In post hoc 2023-2026, the corresponding values were 25 and four of 29 provinces, -5.65 points, and 1,345 pairs (95% interval -7.76 to -3.50). Four school-identity definitions yielded -5.65 to -5.43. Conclusions. The observed maximum in the 15-province fixed panel was in 2023; cutoffs moved later by 2026. This recent direction was stable under alternative school identities and matched examination populations, while its magnitude remained coverage-sensitive. Long hours, a relative-earnings ratio that declined after 2017, lengthy training and varied recruitment requirements describe career context but do not identify causes. Cutoffs describe published filing or admission boundaries, not applicant demand or future physician supply.

after.title: Preprint: Understanding how future-fit the English pre-registration nursing, midwifery and allied health profession curricula are: A mixed methods survey
after.authors: Downey, J.; Varga, M.; Rae, P.; Koroi, M.; Jones, A.; Golder, E.
after.abstract: Background: Health education must respond to changing population needs to ensure healthcare is fit for purpose. Ageing, overwhelmed services, multimorbidity and persistent health inequalities are increasing the need for prevention and community services, whilst digital health is rapidly reshaping how care is delivered. These transformation needs are international, but in 2025 the English NHS 10 Year Plan outlined clear targets with implications for healthcare education. Despite this, little is known about how prepared the current curricula are, therefore, the aim was to explore what curricula are being delivered in English pre-registration programmes. Methods: An online survey of nursing, midwifery and allied health educators in England was undertaken which included fixed-response and open-text questions related to the priority given to digital, community and preventative health compared to other elements of curricula, the volume and format of future-facing curricula, and how to modernise programmes. Data was analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics and content analysis to identify complementary findings and tensions. Results: Of 166 eligible respondents, 31.3% described prevention as a strong component of their course, compared with 21.7% for community and 3.6% for digital health. Few programmes offer dedicated space to cover these elements and over 90% do not use established frameworks to guide the development of education. Open-text accounts described pressures on curriculum space and staff time, alongside the need for educator development, relevant technologies and practice-learning opportunities. Examples of established provision and helpful partnerships showed that experiences varied contingent on a complex interplay of factors. Conclusions: Despite calls to align education with changing health systems, provision remains uneven. Our findings suggest that curricular change cannot be achieved by higher education institutions alone and developing future-proof education requires concurrent alignment of curriculum priorities, educator expertise, practice-learning capacity, and resources across universities, placement providers, regulators, and policymakers.

after.title: Preprint: Automatic cerebral angiographic perfusion analysis
after.authors: Thinzar, L. P.; Sujijantarat, N.; Hebert, R.; Matouk, C. C.; Chung, D.; Wu, O.; Petersen, N. H.; Lyman, K. A.
after.abstract: Purpose: To automate anatomical localization for angiographic perfusion and evaluate agreement with manual processing between biplane projections in a held-out external cohort. Methods: Separate anteroposterior (AP) and lateral projection hemisphere and internal carotid artery (ICA) models used DeepLabv3+ with ResNet50 encoders. Development used patient-separated training, validation, and testing. External patients were excluded from fitting and model selection. Automated pipeline and manual-pipeline perfusion shared downstream calculations. Eligible acquisitions contained at least 7 seconds of data after bolus arrival. Segmentation metrics and Bland-Altman analyses evaluated mean transit time (MTT) and time to maximum of the residue function (Tmax). Results: External segmentation testing included 353 runs from 73 patients. Patient-mean hemisphere Dice was 0.959 (95% CI, 0.952-0.965) in AP and 0.965 (0.960-0.969) in lateral views while ICA Dice was 0.635 (0.617-0.650) and 0.558 (0.534-0.579). Manually processed perfusion comparisons included 165 external runs from 52 patients. Mean absolute differences (95% CI) were 0.39 (0.31-0.47) and 0.32 (0.25-0.40) seconds for AP and lateral MTT, and 0.23 (0.15-0.35) and 0.31 (0.17-0.51) seconds for Tmax. Among 220 external cohort biplane pairs from 61 patients, mean absolute differences were 0.48 seconds (95% CI, 0.42-0.53) for MTT and 0.53 seconds (0.35-0.75) for Tmax. Repeated-measures mean biases (95% CI) were -0.07 (-0.19 to 0.05) and 0.16 seconds (-0.08 to 0.40), with 95% limits of agreement of -1.38 to 1.24 and -2.65 to 2.97 seconds respectively. Conclusion: Our automated perfusion pipeline showed favorable agreement with manually processed results in the external validation cohort. Independently processed biplane views had small average bias.

after.title: Preprint: Continuous at-home wearables and machine learning sensitively track function and progression in pediatric and adult Friedreich's ataxia
after.authors: Arrambide, K.; Yang, F. X.; Farmer, J.; Rai, M.; Profeta, V.; Lynch, D.; Gupta, A. S.
after.abstract: Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA) is the most common hereditary ataxia, characterized by progressive cerebellar and sensory ataxia, proprioceptive loss, and upper motor neuron involvement, with onset typically in childhood. Current outcome measures used in clinical trials are limited by rater subjectivity, coarse scoring, infrequent in-person assessments, and inability to assess behavior continuously in naturalistic settings. We tested whether submovement-based measures derived from accelerometers worn continuously at home could sensitively capture motor impairment and disease progression in FRDA across a range of ages and disease severity. 95 participants (57 FRDA, 38 controls; age 2-75) wore GENEActiv wrist and ankle sensors for one week per timepoint; 60 completed two or more timepoints spanning up to 2.2 years. 85 movement features were extracted including submovement kinematics and activity intensity. The FRDA cohort included ambulatory and non-ambulatory participants spanning early, mid, and late stages of disease. Five machine-learned composite models were evaluated, including FRDA-specific models, and models previously trained on other populations. Sensor measures were evaluated for relationships with clinician-rated and patient-reported measures, reliability, and sensitivity to progression. Ankle sensor measures demonstrated strong cross-sectional correlations with Friedreich's Ataxia-Functional Disability Staging (|r| = 0.66-0.87), Modified Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale total (|r| = 0.53-0.73), Friedreich's Ataxia-Activities of Daily Living (|r| = 0.58-0.74), and Friedreich's Ataxia-Health Index total (|r| = 0.43-0.57), with high within-week reliability (ICC = 0.89-0.96) and large differences between FRDA and control groups (|e.s.| = 2.0-2.6). FRDA-specific composite outcomes showed significant longitudinal sensitivity to disease progression (|MSDR| = 0.67-0.89), whereas patient global impression of change did not capture progression. At-home ankle accelerometer data yield reliable, ecologically valid measures reflecting clinician-rated and patient-reported outcomes, and capture disease progression in FRDA. These results support remote wearables as sensitive digital outcome measures for FRDA clinical trials and disease monitoring.

We tested whether submovement-based measures derived from accelerometers worn continuously at home could sensitively capture motor impairment and disease progression in FRDA across a range of ages and disease severity. 95 participants (57 FRDA, 38 controls; age 2-75) wore GENEActiv wrist and ankle sensors for one week per timepoint; 60 completed two or more timepoints spanning up to 2.2 years. 85 movement features were extracted including submovement kinematics and activity intensity. The FRDA cohort included ambulatory and non-ambulatory participants spanning early, mid, and late stages of disease. Five machine-learned composite models were evaluated, including FRDA-specific models, and models previously trained on other populations. Sensor measures were evaluated for relationships with clinician-rated and patient-reported measures, reliability, and sensitivity to progression. Ankle sensor measures demonstrated strong cross-sectional correlations with Friedreich's Ataxia-Functional Disability Staging (|r| = 0.66-0.87), Modified Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale total (|r| = 0.53-0.73), Friedreich's Ataxia-Activities of Daily Living (|r| = 0.58-0.74), and Friedreich's Ataxia-Health Index total (|r| = 0.43-0.57), with high within-week reliability (ICC = 0.89-0.96) and large differences between FRDA and control groups (|e.s.| = 2.0-2.6). FRDA-specific composite outcomes showed significant longitudinal sensitivity to disease progression (|MSDR| = 0.67-0.89), whereas patient global impression of change did not capture progression. At-home ankle accelerometer data yield reliable, ecologically valid measures reflecting clinician-rated and patient-reported outcomes, and capture disease progression in FRDA. These results support remote wearables as sensitive digital outcome measures for FRDA clinical trials and disease monitoring.

after.title: Preprint: Effects of a High-Airflow Fan-Attached Garment on Thermoregulatory and Physiological Responses During Physical Activity in Hot Environments: A Randomized Crossover Trial
after.authors: Hayashi, K.; Wanifuchi, M.; Ito, H.; Urushizawa, Y.; Tomioka, Y.; Takayama, F.
after.abstract: Objectives: Although fan-attached garments are widely used, conventional airflow rates have shown limited efficacy in suppressing core body temperature elevation during physical activity. We aimed to investigate the effects of a high-airflow fan-attached garment on core body temperature and physiological strain during physical activity in hot environments under different humidity levels. Methods: Seven healthy adult men completed four randomized crossover trials involving two environmental conditions - wet bulb globe temperatures of 25 degrees C (36 degrees C, 20% relative humidity) and 31 degrees C (36 degrees C, 60% relative humidity) - and two garment conditions: control and fan-attached garment (80 L/s airflow). Each trial consisted of a 10-min thermoneutral rest, 10-min hot rest, and 60-min continuous cycle ergometer exercise (60 W). We evaluated rectal and skin temperatures, heart rate, microclimate environment, body mass change, and subjective sensations. Results: At a wet bulb globe temperature of 31 degrees C, the fan-attached garment significantly suppressed the increase in rectal temperature compared with the control garment at 60 min of exercise (difference: 0.50 degrees C, p < 0.001), with rectal temperature remaining unchanged from baseline (+0.11 degrees C, p = 0.077). Exercise heart rate (difference: 31.5 beats/min, p < 0.001) and body mass loss (difference: 0.5 kg, p = 0.001) were also significantly reduced with the fan-attached garment. Microclimate humidity was significantly lower with the fan-attached garment throughout exercise in both environments (p < 0.001). Conclusions: The high-airflow (80 L/s) fan-attached garment effectively prevented an increase in core body temperature and mitigated cardiovascular and thermoregulatory strain during moderate physical activity, even in hot and humid environments.

after.abstract: Accurate, noninvasive diagnosis of malignant nipple discharge remains a longstanding clinical challenge. This study evaluated somatic copy-number variations (CNVs) in nipple discharge DNA (ndDNA) as high-fidelity diagnostic biomarkers and explored their cellular origins and shedding mechanisms. We derived a 20-feature CNV panel from large-scale genomic datasets and validated its diagnostic potential. Integrative single-cell analysis of 50 patients revealed that these features predominantly arose in ancestral states across molecular subtypes and exhibited functionally relevant co-occurrence patterns. In clinical cohorts, ndDNA-based detection achieved 74.4% sensitivity and 94.4% specificity (AUC = 0.863), significantly outperforming plasma cell-free DNA (AUC = 0.517; p < 0.0001). Paired single-cell RNA sequencing confirmed high concordance between ndDNA profiles and malignant epithelial cells. High-fidelity epithelial subclusters displayed active estrogen signaling and distinct immune interactions, and a derived Fidelity Score independently predicted favorable prognosis in two external survival cohorts. Our findings establish nipple discharge as a tumor-proximal liquid biopsy that preserves early tumor genomic signatures with minimal dilution, advancing noninvasive diagnostic and prognostic strategies.

T.; Herold-Mende, C.; Ratliff, M.; Etminan, N.; Krieg, S.; Bunse, L.; Platten, M.; Wick, W.; Wick, A.; von Deimling, A.; Dietrich, S.; Sahm, F.; Suwala, A. K.; Gerstung, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Division of AI in Oncology, German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), Heidelberg, Germany
after.abstract: Glial tumours are the most common primary malignant brain tumours in adults and comprise molecularly and histologically distinct entities with diverse outcomes. Despite this diversity, they arise within a shared anatomical environment, suggesting that common organisational principles may shape tumour heterogeneity. However, how cellular states are organised across gliomas and whether this organisation relates to clinical outcomes remains unclear. To that end, we generated a single-cell resolution spatial transcriptomic atlas of 2.6 million cells from 275 patients spanning IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, IDH-mutant and chromosome 1p/19q codeleted oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant astrocytoma and ependymoma. Across diagnoses, we show how heterogeneous tumour cell states are spatially organised into recurrent neighbourhoods with distinct immune and glial composition, which in turn assemble into a higher-order architecture. Among these cellular neighbourhoods, some, such as the astrocyte-like (AC-like), are conserved across entities, whereas others segregate by clinicopathological parameters. AI-powered histopathology further reveals selective association of neighbourhoods within histological clusters, providing a link between molecular spatial organisation to routine H&E morphology. In astrocytoma, neighbourhood abundance is associated with patient survival independently of WHO grade, with AC-like enrichment linked to favourable outcomes. Same-cell high-plex spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed protein imaging in an independent astrocytoma cohort validated these neighbourhoods and further confirmed enrichment of oligodendrocytes within the TBI neighbourhood. Collectively, our findings reveal that glial tumours are spatially encoded through recurrent multicellular neighbourhoods across different molecular entities, showing clinical relevance beyond conventional histology and providing a foundation for analogous investigation across cancer types.

after.title: Preprint: Hidden Map of the Human Cochlea and the Law of Cochlear Degeneracy
after.authors: Hadj-Allal, Z.; Aarnisalo, A.; Mäkitie, A. A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Helsinki and HUS Helsinki University Hospital
after.abstract: For a century, the pure-tone audiogram has been the foundation of hearing science and otology, routinely assumed to reflect specific cochlear pathology. Here, we resolve the mapping from macroscopic auditory function to microscopic pathology by matching 4.2 million human audiograms against 37 million cochlear states generated using four cochlear model simulators. We show that the audiogram does not specify a unique underlying tissue state: in at least 97.3% of ears, the same audiogram was produced by distinct categories of cochlear cellular lesions. This ambiguity follows two rules, which we formulate as the Law of Cochlear Degeneracy. First, outer and inner hair-cell injuries replace one another only at the same place along the cochlea. Second, only up to a limit: this mutual substitution holds across mild loss but collapses as impairment deepens, and in the tested models outer hair-cell injury alone reaches no more than 44 dB on average. Because the cochlea cannot be biopsied during life, we built a population-scale library of cochlear lesions we call the Hidden Map of the Cochlea, which lists for every audiogram the cellular lesions compatible with it. For any audiogram, the map then names the physiological measurements that tell those lesions apart, a step we call the Cochlear State Differential. Where audiograms are identical, otoacoustic emissions and envelope-following responses separate the underlying cochlear lesions, isolating mechanical amplification loss from sensory transduction injury. Reading the cochlea from the audiogram thus becomes a computable biophysical differential.

after.title: Preprint: Progression and prediction of sensorineural hearing loss in older adults using a convolutional neural network model and Markov chains
after.authors: Matos, H. G. C. d.; Thanis Garrido, S. R.; Alvarenga, K. d. F.; Augusto Pontara da Costa, K.; Jacob, L. C. B.
after.abstract: Objectives: This study compared a convolutional neural network (CNN) and linear regression for predicting mean hearing thresholds at the last audiogram and their variation from the first audiogram. It used audiometric and clinical data from older adults with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Markov chains estimated hearing- loss worsening and stability probabilities between assessments. Analyses considered hypertension, diabetes, occupational noise exposure and age. Design: This retrospective study analysed serial audiograms and clinical records. Data included 823 adults with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Predictive analyses included 394 complete-case records, with 79 records per ear in the independent test set. Cross- validation selected model configurations and evaluated predictive performance across data partitions. Markov chains estimated worsening and stability probabilities across hearing-loss severity categories. Results: CNN achieved cross-validation mean absolute errors of 6.475 dB HL (right ear, RE) and 6.047 dB HL (left ear, LE) and linear regression registered 6.054 dB HL (RE) and 6.170 dB HL (LE). CNN (independent evaluation) showed significantly lower prediction error in the LE after Holm correction (padj = 0.0328). No significant advantage was observed in the RE (padj = 0.1969). Markov state-averaged conditional worsening probabilities were 34.0% (RE) and 35.3% (LE). Observed worsening proportions were 42.2% (RE; 347/823) and 40.9% (LE; 337/823). Corresponding stability probabilities were 57.8% (RE) and 58.6% (LE). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed for occupational noise exposure, hypertension, or diabetes. Worsening estimates increased across age groups. Conclusions: This study provides conditional probabilities of hearing-loss worsening and stability in older adults. CNN predictions and Markov estimates suggest that threshold prediction and severity transitions offer complementary descriptions of hearing changes. The ear-specific CNN advantage warrants further investigation. This characterisation may support assessment of changes in hearing thresholds alongside progression to more severe hearing-loss categories.

after.title: Preprint: Making Invisible Infrastructure Visible: Data Landscapes Across a National Pain and Opioid Research Network through a Qualitative Assessment
after.authors: Adams, M. C. B.; Taylor, R. A.; Hoppe, J. A.; The HD2A Network,
after.author_corresponding_institution: Wake Forest School of Medicine: Wake Forest University School of Medicine
after.abstract: Background Multi-site research networks have become central infrastructure for NIH-supported health research, yet network-level coordination has focused on harmonization, common data models and FAIR principles, while rarely characterizing the heterogeneous data landscapes within a network first. The Helping to End Addiction Long-term(R) Initiative (HEAL Initiative) Data2Action (HD2A) program comprises ten autonomously designed innovation and acceleration projects in opioid use disorder treatment and pain management, with no pre-existing network-level view of what data each project used or how it was governed. Objectives To make the HD2A data-infrastructure landscape visible by systematically characterizing the data environments of all ten projects and identifying cross-project themes, coordination opportunities, and lessons for multi-site networks. Methods Data Infrastructure Support Center staff extracted each project's data-environment characteristics from project documentation into a structured 15-element assessment, which project investigators reviewed and corrected. Two analysts independently coded the ten validated assessments (two-pass inductive content analysis; 19-code codebook), developed six cross-project themes from the coded passages by consensus, and judged each project against them. An investigator reflection survey, summarized descriptively, contextualized the document-based findings. Results Six themes characterized the landscape: all projects integrate multi-source, cross-sector data; dashboards are the common data-to-action venue; adoption of standards-based interoperability is uneven; governance complexity increases nonlinearly with institutional partners; implementation and improvement science frameworks serve as data-quality scaffolding; and sustainability plans depend on institutional transfer. Five synergy clusters were identified. Investigators consistently described data access and governance, not analytic capability, as the binding constraint, and distinguished sustaining technical products from sustaining their use. Conclusions Making a networks data infrastructure visible is not a substitute for harmonization but a prerequisite for deciding how and what to harmonize. HD2As autonomously designed projects share a common structure of constraints, creating opportunities for coordination without uniformity. The structured elicitation approach is replicable in other innovation networks.
